does: Writes the resolved outcome of the interrupts used on one roll into that roll's ConditionRoll: takes the merged eoc::interrupt::RollAdjustments of the roll (ResolvedRoll at +0x48, set flag +0x4C) and the ConditionRoll (StatsRoll at +0x8, Difficulty +0x118), rewrites total, natural, bonus, advantage and criticality, and answers AdjustConditionRollEffectFlags: byte 0 the success against the difficulty flipped, bytes 1-3 advantage, disadvantage, critical. The one place every post-throw change of an attack or spell save by SetRoll, AdjustRoll or SetReroll passes.

evidence.says: the same body as the Toolkit's esv::interrupt::AdjustConditionRoll (returns false unless RollAdjustments+0x4C, visits the StatsRoll alternative of the variant at +0x110, compares Difficulty +0x118 with ResolvedRoll +0x48); called by esv::interrupt::AdjustFunctorConditionRolls, by the spell cast system's adjustment of a cast's rolls (0x334EA80) and by a pass of the passive system (0x32AF420)

a probe saw one call per changed roll after the interrupt was used: SetRoll(20) by the game's Interrupt_MAG_CriticalExecution (natural 15 total 20 -> 20/25 critical), a SetRoll(1) interrupt (17/22 -> 1/6 critical fail), Lucky's SetReroll (3/8 -> 11/16) and Bardic Inspiration on a Sacred Flame save (total 7 -> 8); the roll event had fired 0.4 s earlier with the old values
EoCServer.dll exports this name; it is tied to this function by the job its read shows
the macOS build's symbols hold this name; it is tied to this function by the job its read shows

questions.ask: The passive system's caller 0x32AF420 (ConditionalRollEvent of a passive or status) was not seen calling it: a status's save with an OnPostRoll interrupt unlocked raised no interrupt at all (BIBBERBANG_FUMES). A passive's conditional roll with an interrupt is the way to reach it.
